notes: Table 1 (I:p5-b0) contains 18 entries under “HVSs,” whereas the text counts 16 unbound survey HVSs (T:p6-b0). The difference is the two prior non-survey HVSs, HVS2 (US708) and HVS3 (HE0437-5439); both are retained here as follow-up stars. HVS11, HVS15 and HVS16 were previously identified as unbound and are reclassified as “possible HVSs” (T:p5-b2); they remain follow-up targets because the rules include prior unbound candidates regardless of the current boundness conclusion. HVS20 and HVS21 are described as sitting on the Gnedin threshold but are retained among the five new unbound HVSs (T:p5-b2, T:p6-b7, T:p6-b9). The possible-HVS section is treated as containing retained conditional unbound candidates, since the paper calls them possible HVSs and Figure 3’s caption describes the other possible HVSs as near the Kenyon escape velocity (T:p4-b8). The supplied table transcription appears to span HVS11 over three adjacent rows; because those rows have different coordinates and objects, only the first is HVS11 (SDSS J095906.47+000853.41), and the next two are separate unnumbered possible HVSs. The sole no-reference entry in that possible-HVS group, SDSS J111136.44+005856.44, is matched to the text’s one new possible HVS exceeding the Kenyon model (T:p5-b2) and is listed as candidates_found; SDSS J101359.79+563111.65 is the other unnumbered possible HVS, has prior reference 7, and is retained as follow_up. The “Possible Bound HVSs” are explicitly bound or possibly bound and are not included.

HVS1: RA and Dec are decoded from the SDSS J designation in Table 1; the full Table 2 J2000 coordinates for HVS1 are not displayed. HVS1 is the first HVS from Brown et al. (2005) (Table 1 Ref. 1). The paper explicitly states that v_rf is the minimum Galactic rest-frame velocity, i.e. the radial component and a lower limit, not the full 3D space velocity (T:p6-b0); the current v_rf definition can change earlier values by up to 30 km/s (T:p4-b2). The ≃100 kpc distance is the earlier Brown et al. (2005) value quoted in the Introduction; Table 1 instead gives only R_GC = 76 kpc.

HVS2: The target is HVS2 (= US708, per Table 1). No right ascension or declination is given for HVS2: Table 2 (Appendix) lists coordinates only for the sample portion shown, and US708 is not among those rows, so ra/dec are omitted. No heliocentric distance is reported for HVS2 (only the Galactocentric distance R_GC = 26 kpc in Table 1); Figure 3 plots v_rf vs R for this star but gives no additional numerical distance beyond Table 1. The quoted radial velocity is the heliocentric value v_⊙, and v_rf = 718 km/s is explicitly a rest-frame radial velocity (minimum velocity), not a full 3D speed, so it is recorded as such rather than as a total rest-frame speed. HVS2 is classified in Table 1 among the 16 unbound HVSs, but no per-star bound/unbound probability is reported.

HVS4: HVS4 is listed among the 16 unbound HVSs, but no numerical bound or unbound probability is reported (T:p5-b0; T:p6-b0). The v_rf = 559 km/s value is explicitly a minimum/lower limit to the true velocity, not a full three-dimensional speed (T:p4-b2; T:p5-b0). R_GC = 69 kpc is a Galactocentric radius, not a heliocentric distance (T:p5-b0). The supplied Table 2 excerpt (T:p10-b0) does not show HVS4, so equatorial coordinates are taken from the J2000 SDSS designation in Table 1 (T:p5-b0).

HVS5: Target HVS5 = SDSS J091759.47+672238.35 (Table 1, reference 4 = Brown et al. 2006a). Table 1 also reports v_rf = 664 km/s and g0 = 17.56 mag, M_g = +0.04 mag, l = 146.23 deg, b = +38.70 deg. The v_rf value is not recorded as `galactic_rest_frame_velocity`: the paper states (T:p4-b2) that "v_rf represents the radial component of velocity in the Galactic rest frame, and is thus a lower limit to the true velocity of any HVS", and it is measured relative to the Galactic standard of rest, so it is excluded under the rules for `radial_velocity`. No heliocentric distance, parallax, proper motions, or bound/unbound probabilities are reported for this star (Table 2 of the appendix is truncated and does not include this row). Right ascension and declination are taken from the SDSS J2000 designation given in Table 1 (the coordinate string is the catalog name reported by the authors).

HVS6: HVS6 = SDSS J110557.45+093439.47 (Table 1, reference 5 = Brown et al. 2006b). Table 1 lists v_odot, v_rf, g0 = 18.97 mag, M_g = +0.10 mag, R_GC = 61 kpc, l = 243.12 deg, b = +59.56 deg; only the velocities and Galactocentric radius are among the requested quantities. The authors state v_rf is the radial component in the Galactic rest frame and a lower limit to the star's true velocity, so the galactic_rest_frame_velocity entry is recorded as a lower bound. Coordinates (R.A., Decl.) for this star appear only in the machine-readable Table 2 (only a 10-row portion of the full 955-star table is shown in the supplied material), so no equatorial position or parallax/heliocentric distance is available. No bound/unbound probability is reported for individual stars.

HVS7: Target HVS7 = SDSS J113312.12+010824.87. It is the open magenta star labeled "7" in Figure 3, at R ≈ 37 kpc and v_rf ≈ 396 km/s. The paper explicitly defines v_rf as the radial component in the Galactic rest frame and a lower limit to the true 3D velocity, so it is recorded here as a lower bound on galactic_rest_frame_velocity rather than as a total speed. No uncertainty is given for HVS7's velocity or distance in Table 1. Section 3.2 says HVS7 changed "from 60 kpc to 37 kpc" and that echelle spectroscopy gives ≃60 kpc; because the supplied text does not clearly distinguish heliocentric from Galactocentric distance for the 60 kpc value, both R_GC = 37 kpc (Table 1) and 60 kpc (prior/echelle estimate) are recorded, with the ambiguity noted. The joint HVS7/HVS8 statement R ≃ 50 kpc is also recorded. HVS7 is classified among the 16 unbound HVSs and called "almost certainly" an HVS, but no bound/unbound probability is reported.

HVS8: The HVS8 row in Table 1 gives v_rf = 393 km/s, but the paper defines v_rf as the radial component/minimum Galactic rest-frame velocity, not the total three-dimensional Galactic rest-frame speed, so it is not recorded as galactic_rest_frame_velocity (definition in T:p4-b2 and T:p6-b0). HVS8 is classified as an unbound HVS, but no bound or unbound probability is reported. No heliocentric distance, parallax, or proper motion is reported for HVS8 in the supplied material. The right ascension and declination are taken from the J2000 SDSS identifier in Table 1 (T:p5-b0).

HVS9: Target is HVS9 / SDSS J102137.08-005234.77, listed in the "HVSs" section of Table 1 (also plotted as an open magenta star in Fig. 3). RA and Dec are taken directly from the SDSS designation reported in Table 1 (J2000, sexagesimal sexagesimal notation retained; no conversion performed); the full Table 2 entry for this star is not included in the supplied excerpt, so no separate coordinate columns exist for it in the materials. Table 1 gives only the Galactocentric distance R_GC = 47 kpc, not a heliocentric distance, so no `distance` value is recorded. The Galactic rest-frame value 461 km/s is the paper's v_rf, which the authors explicitly define as the radial component in the Galactic rest frame and a lower limit to the true space velocity, so it is recorded as a lower bound rather than a total 3D speed. No parallax, proper motion, or bound/unbound probability is reported for this star.

HVS10: For HVS10, Table 1 gives v_⊙ = 478 km/s, v_rf = 423 km/s, R_GC = 66 kpc, and catalog SDSS J120337.85+180250.35 (T:p5-b0). The excerpted Table 2 does not list HVS10; its RA/Dec are read from this supplied SDSS J2000 designation. The paper states v_rf is the Galactic rest-frame radial component, not a full space velocity and a lower limit to the true velocity, so it is recorded only as a lower bound on galactic_rest_frame_velocity. No parallax, proper motion, heliocentric distance, or bound/unbound probability is reported for HVS10 in the supplied material.

HVS12: The HVS12 row in Table 1 (T:p5-b0) provides the velocities, magnitude, Galactocentric distance, Galactic coordinates, and SDSS catalog name. No separate J2000 coordinates are given for HVS12; the right ascension and declination were parsed from the catalog designation SDSS J105009.59+031550.67. The v_rf value is explicitly identified as a lower limit to the true velocity (T:p4-b2), so it is recorded as a lower bound on the total Galactic rest-frame speed rather than as a full space velocity.

HVS13: HVS13 is identified as SDSS J105248.30-000133.94. Its RA and Dec are read from this SDSS catalog identifier because the supplied HVS13 row does not explicitly tabulate J2000 coordinates. Table 1 gives no uncertainties for v_odot, v_rf, or R_GC. The v_rf = 421 km/s value is retained only as a lower bound on the total Galactic rest-frame speed; it is not used as radial_velocity because radial_velocity excludes velocities relative to the Galactic standard of rest. No heliocentric distance, parallax, proper motions, or bound/unbound probabilities are reported for HVS13 in the supplied material.

HVS14: The supplied excerpt does not give a separate RA/Dec row for HVS14; the coordinates are taken from its reported SDSS designation SDSS J104401.75+061139.02. The paper's v_rf=396 km/s is explicitly the radial component in the Galactic rest frame and a lower limit to the total space velocity, not the total three-dimensional speed. No heliocentric distance, parallax, proper motions, or numerical bound/unbound probabilities are reported for HVS14 in the supplied material.

HVS15: HVS15 is listed in Table 1 under Possible HVSs (T:p5-b0) and is reclassified as a possible HVS because it is above the Kenyon et al. (2008) threshold but below the Gnedin et al. (2010) threshold (T:p5-b2). Its v_rf=322 km/s is explicitly the minimum Galactic rest-frame velocity/radial component and a lower limit to the true velocity, not a total three-dimensional speed (T:p4-b2, T:p6-b0); therefore it is not recorded as galactic_rest_frame_velocity.
